results.name: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your hand on it at shoulder height with your arm straight.
Rotate your thumb downward.
Turn your body gently away from the wall until you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your arm straight.
Breathe steadily.
results.description: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Chest.

results.name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and find a stable surface to hold onto for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and bring your heel towards your glutes. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand.
Keep your knees close together and lightly pull your right ankle upward, feeling a stretch along the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release your right ankle and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the left leg.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
results.description: Standing Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and place the heel of one foot on a low step or out in front of you with the leg straight.
Keep your back flat.
Hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch in the back of that leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep the standing knee soft.
Lead with your chest.
results.description: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Band Bent Over One Arm Kickback
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place one end of the resistance band under your feet. Hold the other end of the band in your right hand and bend your torso forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your knees bent.
Position your right upper arm almost parallel to the floor with your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle, keeping your upper arm close to your body.
Extend your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your right arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you extend your arm back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Band Bent Over One Arm Kickback is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Band Incline Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle. Place the resistance band under the bench and hold one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight above your head, palms facing forward.
Lower the handles behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring your forearms are parallel to the floor and your upper arms remain still.
Extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored under the bench to avoid slipping.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to reduce strain on your joints. 3 .Focus on squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
results.description: Band Incline Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category.

results.name: Band Lying Press Down
instructions: Attach a resistance band at the bottom of a piece of sturdy equipment.
Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Hold onto the resistance bands with your hands above your forehead, elbows bent and facing upward.
Push the band up to the ceiling, squeezing your triceps hard at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back in a neutral position throughout the exercise.
Keep your arms perpendicular to the ground and elbows tucked in.
Keep the movement controlled and avoid letting the band pull your arms back quickly.
Exhale as you extend the band upward using your triceps and inhale as you return.
results.description: Band Lying Press Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in the knees, facing the anchored resistance band.
Using an overhand grip, grasp the other end of the band, keeping your elbow bent and tucked close to your side.
Press downward by squeezing your triceps, extending your arm at the elbow joint. Pause briefly at the bottom of the exercise.
Slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired amount of repetitions and switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow close to your torso throughout the movement and upper arm stationary, moving only at the elbow joint.
Fully extend your arm without forcefully locking your elbow. Control the return phase to maintain constant tension on the band.
Stand tall with your chest up and core engaged to prevent body sway.
Exhale as you press downward and inhale as you return.
results.description: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Barbell Lying Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your elbows, bringing the barbell towards over your forehead.
When the barbell is behind your head, reverse the movement by extending your elbows to return the barbell to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment throughout the movement.
results.description: Barbell Lying Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Barbell Lying Triceps Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your elbows, bringing the barbell towards your forehead.
When the barbell is just above your forehead, reverse the movement by extending your elbows to return the barbell to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment throughout the movement.
results.description: Barbell Lying Triceps Skull Crusher is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Cable Cross Pushdown
instructions: Stand upright between two high cable pulleys and hold each handle in the opposite hand.Bend your elbows so that the handles are crossing in front of your chest.
Extend your elbows to press the handles down and outward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly while squeezing your triceps at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly bend your elbows to return the handles to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your sides throughout the exercise.
Move only at your elbows and avoid swinging your shoulders.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Inhale as you return to the starting position and exhale as you press the handles downward.
results.description: Cable Cross Pushdown is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms, Core.
